why_naive_bound_is_not_proof: Each equation's 'bit budget' (log2(A)) is an UPPER bound on how many bits of unknown-material information it can reveal, not a guarantee. Equations that touch a chain position for the first time introduce a brand-new, previously-unconstrained latent chain value (u^(i)_k) at the SAME time as they touch a point of S -- so many early-position equations are consistent with many (S-point, u-value) pairs simultaneously and reveal close to ZERO net bits until later equations cross-link the same S domain point from a different chain path. Whether that cross-linking happens frequently enough to pin down S is an empirical question about the search space, not something the raw bit count can settle.

4. overdetermined_multiple_equivalent: more than one tuple fits all M known pairs, but    all surviving candidates agree on the unseen target (functional equivalence for    decryption purposes even though the raw material differs).
5. computationally_hard_despite_overdetermined: a unique/near-unique solution may exist    in principle, but no tractable search method was available to find it within budget.
